title: Conquest of Sylhet
subtitle: The Sylhet campaign associated with Shah Jalal and Sikandar Khan Ghazi.
summary: The conquest of Sylhet is commonly associated with the expansion of Muslim political and spiritual networks into the Sylhet region around 1303, with Shah Jalal central to later memory. The event is historically important, but details of chronology and military sequence depend on later traditions as well as regional histories.
heroTagline: Conquest of Sylhet reshaped power and governance patterns in Bengal.
whyItMatters: Sylhet's conquest matters because it links frontier politics, Sufi memory, and regional incorporation into wider Bengal histories. It should be read with care because hagiographic traditions and later narratives shape much of the public memory.
longTermLegacy: The episode made Sylhet a durable site of Islamic sacred geography and regional identity, while also raising source-critical questions about how conquest memories are preserved.
identityMemoryNotes: Shah Jalal's memory remains central to Sylhet's religious and regional identity, but precise event details should be framed as historically layered rather than simple fact.
